8 For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come. (1 Timothy 4:8 KJV)

Paul is not saying that physical exercise is not profitable at all, but he is saying that spiritual exercise and godliness are much more beneficial to our bodies and spirits, therefore godliness will not only benefit our physical bodies, but will be of great benefit to our spiritual being. Exercising our bodies only helps in this life, but living a godly life will benefit us now and for eternity. As with physical exercise, living godly cannot be of much value unless we are consistent in doing it (1 Peter 1:15). You can not just visit godliness once in a while and expect much benefit, the same as you can not exercise the body only once in a while and expect much benefit.

It has been shown many times that prayer and godly living, not only helps the spirit, but also benefits the human body. As it says in Proverbs 17:22 â€œA merry heart doeth good like a medicineâ€, and to have a merry heart you must be a disciple indeed (John 8:31). The way to have a merry heart is to live for God, and He will give you the peace and joy that causes a merry heart, as it is part of the fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23). Thank you Lord for giving us instructions on how to live a blessed life.
